page: Vultr vc2-1c-0.5gb is an entry-tier virtual server within the Cloud Compute family, configured for minimal resource requirements. It features one shared Intel x86_64 vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz with one hardware thread, backed by 32 KB of L1d cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while advanced matrix extensions and AVX-512 are not present. System memory is restricted to 0.5 GB, and storage is provided by a bundled 10 GB NVMe SSD. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no GPU accelerators are included.

In benchmark evaluations, the hardware configuration demonstrates baseline compute capabilities consistent with its single shared core. The server recorded 483.45 in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside an overall PassMark CPU score of 666.74. Cryptographic and extended instruction benchmarks scored 203.47 and 348.68 respectively. Cached small-block memory bandwidth reached 45.49 GB/sec. Operational throughput tests registered 0.56 million Redis SET operations per second and 0.86 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The tight 0.5 GB memory capacity limits software execution to minimal footprints, requiring careful management of operating system overhead. The shared vCPU model also introduces susceptibility to multi-tenant CPU competition. Despite these performance ceilings, the configuration offers high qualitative cost efficiency for baseline workloads that do not demand persistent compute or extensive memory pools. The instance is suited for lightweight automation, simple cron triggers, low-traffic static web serving, DNS resolution, and jump boxes.
description: The Vultr vc2-1c-0.5gb is an entry-level virtual server in the Cloud Compute product line, architected for low-demand computing tasks. It is configured with 1 shared Intel x86_64 vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz, 0.5 GB of system memory, and a 10 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. The platform includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without GPU hardware acceleration. Benchmark evaluations reflect its minimal resource footprint, with stress-ng single and multi-core scores registering at 483.45, a PassMark CPU score of 666.74, and memory read throughput of 45.49 GB/sec on cached small blocks. Network and service throughput include 0.86 GB/sec in static web serving and 0.56 million Redis SET operations per second. Given the limited RAM allocation and shared vCPU model, this instance is suited for lightweight utility services, single-purpose automation scripts, minimal web endpoints, and low-traffic bastion hosts where low infrastructure footprint is preferred over compute density.
